newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy industrialists say budget must be structural.
newsitem.headline: Italy industrialists say budget must be structural.

text.p: Italy's forthcoming mini-budget must be based on structural measures, but some tax hikes might be acceptable, Gianpaolo Galli, head of research at industrialists' organisation Confindustria said on Tuesday.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has indicated that the planned budget will cut around 14 trillion lire off the deficit this year, adding that this should be enough to secure Italy a place at the launch of the single European currency.

Galli told Reuters that only a package of around 20 trillion lire would suffice to cut Italy's state deficit to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP), as required by the Maastricht Treaty for EMU aspirants.
"We can accept fiscal measures but only on condition that the majority of the (budget) is heavily aimed at reducing costs," Galli said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said he wants the budget to be based largely on structural measures but has run into opposition from government ally the Communist Refoundation, which is against cuts to welfare spending.

Galli said the only way to secure lasting budget reductions was to slice back at pensions, health spending and state salaries, saying that these three items made up 80 percent of government spending net of interest payments.
"We don't just have to get the three percent deficit/GDP level in 1997, but every year thereafter," Galli said.
"Imagine what would happen if there were some global economic crisis and we did not have structural budget measures in place," he added. -- Crispian Balmer +396 6782501
